Clan: @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.oWsHHlI3OS7cwvaF]{Ravnos} (clan-specific; may not be taken by outsiders at character creation)

The Path of Paradox teaches that all existence is fluid and malleable. Nothing is permanent or real. The universe is an ever-shifting vortex, and all in it is composed of variable amounts of ethereal matter, called "weig." Ravnos on this Path gradually learn their raison d'etre: to destroy the blasphemous creation of the Antediluvians, that thing known as reality. They learn to harness their internal weig for the production of reality-altering effects — mere illusions at low levels of power, but as the Ravnos becomes more powerful, the "tricks" gradually increase in potency.

Ravnos also actively attempt to alter others' perceptions of reality, favoring trickery and theft. Ultimately, however, the weig must be released into the vortex; advanced students of this Path actively seek out items that retain weig — "magic" items, Lupine fetishes, and the like — and destroy them. The most powerful followers hunt vampires with great amounts of weig: low generation, and the lower the better.

Hierarchy of Sins (most to least severe):

  1. Refusing to commit diablerie upon an elder of another clan.
  2. Refusing to lead a "locked" being into the light — or into destruction.
  3. Showing any concern for mortals.
  4. Failing to acquire items or knowledge that would affect Gehenna.
  5. Failing to trick others when the opportunity arises.
  6. Being caught altering another's reality via the select redistribution of possessions (known among the vulgar as stealing).
  7. Refusing to release the weig of an empowered device.
  8. Joining another sect (@UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.sects.JournalEntry.fc464242d84d4e34]{Camarilla} or @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.sects.JournalEntry.6868ee8c357f4b73]{Sabbat}) and actively maintaining the existing structure thereof.
  9. Actively hindering change.
  10. Actively inducing boredom.

Path Traits:

  • Release — Frenzy whenever you are prevented from committing diablerie on an elder of another clan, or releasing the weig from any contained item.
  • Concern — Frenzy if you must watch Kindred pamper or care for unenlightened mortals.
  • Knowledge — Frenzy whenever someone directly prevents you from acquiring knowledge of Gehenna.
  • Failure — Frenzy if you are caught trying to pull a heist of any sort, whether a simple riddle, trick, or theft.
  • Boredom — You'll frenzy just to shake things up if your character is bored during the evening's session.
